title: Live animal calcium imaging of the geniculate ganglion
protocol: Attach the Gaymar T/Pump with the warming pad and fill it with water.
Turn on the pump to pre-warm the warming pad.
Weigh the mouse.
Prepare the anesthetic: add 2.4 ul of ketamine per gram of body weight, 1ul of xylazine per gram of body weight, and sterile 0.9% NaCl solution to a final volume of 200 ul (solution A).
Add 2.4 ul of ketamine per gram of body weight and 0.9% NaCl solution to a final volume of 200 ul (solution B).
Inject Solution A for the initial anesthesia.
After 1 hour, inject 50 ul of solution B every 30 min or as needed.
Use paw pinch reflex to test whether more anesthesia is required.
For example: for a mouse of 25 grams, mix 60ul ketamine and 25 ul xylazine, and add 115 ul 0.9% NaCl solution to make 200 ul of solution A.
Mix 60 ul ketamine and 140 ul 0.9% NaCl solution to make 200 ul of solution B.
Inject 100 ul of solution A (i.p.) with a 1ml syringe and 30G needle.
Start the timer right after the injection (T=0min).
The mouse should become anesthetized in 3 min.
Transfer the mouse onto the warming pad at T=3min.
Mount the mouse to the nose-holder at T=10min in a supine position.
Insert the rectal probe to monitor body temperature.
Adjust Gaymar T/Pump to maintain the mouse's body temperature at 37 degrees.
Rinse the tongue with artificial saliva every 5-10min during surgery.
Pinch the mouse paw to check if the mouse is fully anesthetized at T=15min.
Wait until the mouse loses the pinch reflex before beginning surgery.
Apply mineral oil to the neck and upper chest area.
Make a 1 cm midline incision to expose the salivary glands.
Separate the two lobes of the salivary glands with blunt dissection.
Blunt dissect the trachea muscle to expose the trachea.
Make a horizontal cut in the trachea without cutting it completely through.
Insert the tracheal cannula about 0.5 cm into the trachea.
Locate the esophagus underneath the trachea and separate it from surrounding tissue.
Place a suture thread underneath the esophagus.
Make a horizontal cut in the esophagus caudal to the thread without cutting through completely.
Insert the esophageal tube into the oral cavity between the tongue and palate.
Gently press the tube through the throat until the end of the tube exits the incision made in step 7.
Pull the tube out through the incision until a pad lies between the tongue and palate.
Tighten the suture around the incision to fix the tube in place.
Retract the skin and trachea to expose the digastric muscle on the left side using a 3cm Goldstein retractor.
Separate the tendon of the digastric muscle slightly.
Cauterize the tendon to detach the caudal part of the digastric muscle.
Blunt dissect the hyoglossus muscle to expose the tympanic bulla.
Clean the muscles and connective tissue around the tympanic bulla area.
Retract the jaw rostrally with the hook to enlarge the area above the tympanic bulla.
Using #2 Inox forceps, break the transparent portion of the bulla.
Break the opaque part of the bulla using #2 Inox forceps.
Be careful not to damage the tympanic membrane while breaking the bulla.
Remove the stapes of the ossicles with #5 Inox forceps.
Cut the tendon connecting the tensor tympani muscle to the ossicles with #55 Inox forceps.
Grasp and remove the tensor tympani muscle with #55 Inox forceps.
Attach suction pipette I to the vacuum.
Use the suction pipette to remove tissue fluid and blood.
Carefully grasp and completely remove any remaining parts of the tensor tympani muscle.
Rotate the mouse and the stage to a horizontal position (clockwise 90 degrees) to enable a better view of the tympanic cavity.
Break and remove the cochlear promontory using forceps.
Remove tissue fluid and blood by suction pipette.
Continuously remove tissue fluid as it appears during surgery.
Use #5 carbon steel forceps to break the temporal bone along the edges of GG, inside the dashed red lines in fig 13 to avoid blood vessels.
Remove the bone by breaking into large fragments.
If there is bleeding around the GG, remove the blood with small pieces of kimwipe.
Use #5SF Inox forceps to remove the bone fragments directly over the GG (fig14).
Do not touch the ganglion with forceps.
Remove the fluid with suction pipette continuously.
Tighten the ear bars and the nose clamp.
Install suction pipette II close to the geniculate ganglion.
Fix the suction pipette by taping it to the head holder.
Transfer the mouse with the warming pad to the confocal microscope.
Fix the stage under the confocal microscope.
Connect suction micropipette II to vacuum.
Locate the geniculate ganglion using epifluorescence with a DAPI filter and a 4x objective.
Check the fluorescence of geniculate ganglion neurons using the 20x long working distance objective.
Use the 488nm laser at 30% power to scan the geniculate ganglion.
Set the pinhole at 400 um.
Adjust hv around 600-700.
Load taste solutions into reservoirs of the perfusion system.
Connect the perfusion manifold to the esophageal tube.
Place a suction tube close to the mouth of the mouse to withdraw taste solutions.
Record fluorescence at a scanning speed of approximately 300 ms/scan using Olympus’ Fluoview software.
Perfuse taste solutions into the oral cavity.
